content:
The [Image Resizer](/image-resizer) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Resize JPG, PNG and WebP images privately in your browser. Open it and start straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like. It is one of the [Image & Media tools](/tools?category=Image%20%26%20Media) on CalcHub — the others work the same way.

Resize an image to exact pixel dimensions or a percentage of its original size, preserve its aspect ratio and download the result. Your image is processed locally with your browser's canvas and is never uploaded. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers. Related Image & Media tools include [QR Code Generator](/qr-code-generator), [Aspect Ratio Calculator](/aspect-ratio-calculator) and [Color Code Converter](/color-code-converter).

## How to use the Image Resizer

Open the [Image Resizer](/image-resizer) and start straight away — there is no form to fill in first. The result updates as you work, so you can try different settings and see the change straight away.

1. Check the result — it updates instantly as you type.
2. Use Reset to start over with the default values.

## Formula

New height = new width ÷ original aspect ratio when Lock aspect ratio is enabled.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Image Resizer](/image-resizer) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic. If the figures look wrong, check your inputs first — a misplaced decimal point is the usual culprit.

The steps are the same whatever numbers you use; only the figures change.

## Trying it out

The fastest way to see what the [Image Resizer](/image-resizer) does is to open it and enter values you already know the answer for. Change one input at a time and watch how the result responds — that tells you more than any description. Everything runs in your browser, so you can experiment freely: nothing is saved, sent or tracked.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Use WebP for a smaller web-ready file.
- Resizing upward cannot restore detail that is not in the original.
- Your original file is never changed.

Keep these in mind and the figures will be as useful as the numbers you put in.

## Frequently asked questions

### Are my images uploaded?

No. Resizing and export happen entirely in your browser. Try it with your own numbers in the [Image Resizer](/image-resizer) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Which formats can I download?

You can export JPG, PNG or WebP, subject to your browser's canvas support. Try it with your own numbers in the [Image Resizer](/image-resizer) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What formula does the Image Resizer use?

New height = new width ÷ original aspect ratio when Lock aspect ratio is enabled. You can see it in action in the [Image Resizer](/image-resizer) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.

### Is the Image Resizer free to use?

Yes. The Image Resizer is free to use as often as you like, with no sign-up. There is no limit on how often you use it, nothing to install, and no account to create — open the [Image Resizer](/image-resizer) and start straight away.
